title: Reentrancy Safety (State Consistency Across External-Call Boundaries)

cwe: CWE-841 Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow

dascp.note: Prevents the reentrant-double-spend mode at the contract-execution layer; does not establish the broader settlement-level encumbrance (a no-double-spend-until-settled property is tracked as a gap).

descriptions.semantic: When a contract makes an external call (which may hand control to untrusted code), no re-entrant invocation can observe or exploit a transiently inconsistent internal state to extract value or violate an invariant. The externally observable effect of each invocation is equivalent to some execution in which the invocation completed before any nested re-entry began.
descriptions.system_theoretic: Two complementary readings. (1) LOCK reading — a mutual-exclusion safety invariant: the guarded critical region is never concurrently active in two stack frames. (2) ATOMICITY reading — a 2-safety hyperproperty: the interleaved (re-entrant) execution is observationally equivalent to a serialized one, i.e. nested frames do not interfere. The lock reading is a sound (stronger) approximation of the atomicity reading.
descriptions.security: Defends every contract that performs an external call while holding unsettled internal accounting (balances marked-for-payout, shares pending burn, oracle reads pending update). Violation is value extraction by recursive re-entry (classic same-function), by entering a sibling function (cross-function), by re-entering across contracts (cross-contract), or by reading stale state during the callback window (read-only reentrancy).
descriptions.execution_semantics: Manifests at CALL/DELEGATECALL/STATICCALL boundaries and at ERC-20/721/777/1155 transfer hooks that yield control to the recipient. The violation window is the interval between an external call and the settlement of the state changes it logically depends on. Effects-before-interactions collapses this window to empty.
descriptions.formal_verification: The lock formulation is a 1-safety state invariant, directly SMT-/symbolic-checkable. The atomicity formulation is a 2-safety hyperproperty requiring self-composition (compare the re-entrant schedule against the serialized one) or an invariant asserting the critical state predicate holds at every external-call site.

formalization.signature: State s; predicate inGuarded(s): the mutex is held; CriticalInv(s): the contract's value-accounting invariant. External-call sites are distinguished transition labels callₖ.
formalization.first_order_logic:
Lock safety:  ∀ reachable s . ¬( inGuarded(s) ∧ aboutToEnterGuarded(s) ).
Effects-before-interactions:  ∀ external-call site callₖ . CriticalInv holds in the pre-state of callₖ  (i.e. all state mutations the call depends on are already committed).

temporal_logic.ltl: G( externalCall → CriticalInv )   and   G( enterGuarded → ¬locked )  with  locked toggled across the region.

hoare.command: withdraw(): effects; lock; external call; unlock

formalization.state_machine: A two-token mutex automaton composed with the contract LTS: states {free, held}; entering the guarded region requires `free`, sets `held`; any transition attempting to enter the guarded region from `held` is absent from the LTS. The property asserts no such absent edge is reachable.
formalization.type_theoretic: Re-entrancy safety corresponds to a uniqueness/affine-resource discipline: the right to be inside the critical region is a non-duplicable token; an external call temporarily relinquishes no claim on committed state. In separation-logic terms, the call site frames out the contract's invariant-bearing footprint so callee code cannot touch it.
formalization.hyperproperty: Atomicity = observational equivalence between the re-entrant interleaving and a serial schedule; a 2-safety property verifiable by self-composition of the call graph.

relationships.note: A reentrant mint/credit callback must not bypass the supply guard or double-credit.
Reentrancy is a principal mechanism by which conservation-of-value is broken (double withdrawal).
Atomic failure rollback isolates the ATOMICITY reading of this record — the state cutoff on failure — and says nothing about callback-boundary consistency.

Callback settlement integrity refines the CALL-SITE-CONSISTENCY reading, adding the explicit pending claim covering the custody gap and its exactly-once consumption. A post-callback storage cutoff covers only part of this record's atomicity reading and should not be reported as covering either refinement in full.

attack_surface.pattern: external call before balance decrement; callee recursively re-enters withdraw
incident_refs: The DAO (2016) — VERIFIED historical incident, canonical example
attack_surface.notes: Closed by effects-before-interactions and/or a nonReentrant mutex.

attack_surface.pattern: callback enters a sibling function that shares the inconsistent state
attack_surface.notes: A per-function lock is insufficient; the guard must cover the shared-state group.

attack_surface.pattern: during the callback window a view function returns stale state, mispricing a dependent protocol
incident_refs: UNVERIFIED: multiple DeFi oracle/price read-only reentrancy findings
attack_surface.notes: View functions are not write-protected by a mutex; consumers must read post-settlement or use reentrancy-aware getters.

attack_surface.pattern: shared mutable state across contracts re-entered via a third contract
attack_surface.notes: Requires reasoning about the whole trust cluster, not a single contract.

metrics: max call-stack depth into guarded regions
count of external calls preceding state settlement
invariant_checkpoints: CriticalInv asserted at every external-call site pre-state

strategies.notes: Prove CriticalInv holds in the pre-state of every external call; covers cross-function/read-only variants the mutex-only check misses.
Flags state writes after external calls; high recall, some false positives.

testability: malicious receiver that re-enters reverts or cannot gain
balance conserved under randomized re-entrant callbacks (Echidna handler)

runtime: nonReentrant mutex (covering the full shared-state group)

assumptions.statement: The mutex storage cannot be reset out-of-band by a delegatecall/storage-collision path.

provenance.notes: Lock formulation soundly over-approximates atomicity; record both so verifiers can choose.
